62005-an-account-of-the-ladies-of-llango.title: An Account Of The Ladies Of Llangollen
62005-an-account-of-the-ladies-of-llango.creator: Unknown
62005-an-account-of-the-ladies-of-llango.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. , accordingly, purchased the estate, built a new cottage on the site of the old one, laid out gardens, pleasure grounds, rural walks and bridges, by which they might enjoy the natural charms of this picturesque retreat. Their mode of life being very singular, and their costume still more so, they soon became noticed by the many travellers who passed through North Wales.

arxiv-1507-08181.title: Schwartz-Zippel Bounds for Two-dimensional Products
arxiv-1507-08181.creator: Frank de Zeeuw
arxiv-1507-08181.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Frank de Zeeuw. We prove bounds on intersections of algebraic varieties in ℂ 4 \mathbb{C}^{4} with Cartesian products of finite sets from ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2} , and we point out connections with several classic theorems from combinatorial geometry.

arxiv-1603-01710.title: Locally toroidal polytopes of rank 6 and sporadic groups
arxiv-1603-01710.creator: Dmitrii V. Pasechnik
arxiv-1603-01710.description: Abstract . We augment the list of finite universal locally toroidal regular polytopes of type { 3 , 3 , 4 , 3 , 3 } \{3,3,4,3,3\} due to P. McMullen and E. Schulte, adding as well as removing entries. This disproves a related long-standing conjecture.

arxiv-2103-16855.title: Breaking Cassie’s law for condensation in a nano-patterned slit
arxiv-2103-16855.creator: Martin Láska, Andrew O. Parry, Alexandr Malijevský
arxiv-2103-16855.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Martin Láska, Andrew O. Parry, Alexandr Malijevský. We study the phase transitions of a fluid confined in a capillary slit made from two adjacent walls each of which are a periodic composite of stripes of two different materials. For wide slits the capillary condensation occurs at a pressure which is described accurately by a combination of the Kelvin equation and the Cassie law for an averaged contact angle.

arxiv-2203-14843.title: Doodle It Yourself: Class Incremental Learning by Drawing a Few Sketches
arxiv-2203-14843.creator: Ayan Kumar Bhunia Viswanatha Reddy Gajjala Subhadeep Koley Rohit Kundu, Aneeshan Sain Tao Xiang Yi-Zhe Song
arxiv-2203-14843.description: Abstract The human visual system is remarkable in learning new visual concepts from just a few examples. This is precisely the goal behind few-shot class incremental learning (FSCIL), where the emphasis is additionally placed on ensuring the model does not suffer from “forgetting”.

arxiv-2209-13422.title: Efficient On-Device Session-Based Recommendation Journal: TOIS Volume: 1 1 1 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Thanks: This work was supported by the Australian Research Council Future Fellowship (Grant No. FT210100624), the Discovery Project (Grant No. DP190101985), and the Discovery Early Career
arxiv-2209-13422.creator: Xin Xia, Junliang Yu, Qinyong Wang, Chaoqun Yang, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin
arxiv-2209-13422.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Xin Xia, Junliang Yu, Qinyong Wang, Chaoqun Yang, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin. On-device session-based recommendation systems have been achieving increasing attention on account of the low energy/resource consumption and privacy protection while providing promising recommendation performance. To fit the powerful neural session-based recommendation models in resource-constrained mobile devices, tensor-train decomposition and its variants have been widely applied to reduce memory footprint by decomposing the embedding table into smaller tensors, showing great potential in compressing recommendation models.

arxiv-2307-02179.title: Open-Source LLMs for Text Annotation: A Practical Guide for Model Setting and Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2307-02179.creator: Meysam Alizadeh, Maël Kubli, Zeynab Samei, Shirin Dehghani, Mohammadmasiha Zahedivafa, Juan D. Bermeo, Maria Korobeynikova, Fabrizio Gilardi
arxiv-2307-02179.description: Abstract This paper studies the performance of open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) in text classification tasks typical for political science research. By examining tasks like stance, topic, and relevance classification, we aim to guide scholars in making informed decisions about their use of LLMs for text analysis.

arxiv-2310-18415.title: Overture POI data for the United Kingdom: a comprehensive, queryable open data product
arxiv-2310-18415.creator: Patrick Ballantyne
arxiv-2310-18415.description: Abstract Point of Interest data that is comprehensive, globally-available and open-access, is sparse, despite being important inputs for research in a number of application areas. New data from the Overture Maps Foundation offers significant potential in this arena, but accessing the data relies on computational resources beyond the skillset and capacity of the average researcher.

arxiv-2311-18836.title: ChatPose: Chatting about 3D Human Pose
arxiv-2311-18836.creator: Yao Feng Jing Lin Sai Kumar Dwivedi Yu Sun Priyanka Patel Michael J. Black, [0.25mm] Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems - Tübingen ETH Zürich, Meshcapade Tsinghua University
arxiv-2311-18836.description: Abstract We introduce ChatPose, a framework employing Large Language Models (LLMs) to understand and reason about 3D human poses from images or textual descriptions. Our work is motivated by the human ability to intuitively understand postures from a single image or a brief description, a process that intertwines image interpretation, world knowledge, and an understanding of body language.

arxiv-2312-04427.title: Spheroidal Molecular Communication via Diffusion: Signaling Between Homogeneous Cell Aggregates This work was supported by the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council [grant number EP/V030493/1]. For the purpose of open access, the authors have applied a Creative Commons Attribution (CC-B
arxiv-2312-04427.creator: Mitra Rezaei, Hamidreza Arjmandi, Mohammad Zoofaghari, Kajsa Kanebratt, Liisa Vilén, David Janzen, Peter Gennemark, and Adam Noel
arxiv-2312-04427.description: Abstract Recent molecular communication (MC) research has integrated more detailed computational models to capture the dynamics of practical biophysical systems. This paper focuses on developing realistic models for MC transceivers inspired by spheroids – three-dimensional cell aggregates commonly used in organ-on-chip experimental systems.

arxiv-2409-12535.title: Deep Probability Segmentation: Are segmentation models probability estimators?
arxiv-2409-12535.creator: Simone Fassio, Simone Monaco, Daniele Apiletti
arxiv-2409-12535.description: Abstract Deep learning has revolutionized various fields by enabling highly accurate predictions and estimates. One important application is probabilistic prediction, where models estimate the probability of events rather than deterministic outcomes. This approach is particularly relevant and, therefore, still unexplored for segmentation tasks where each pixel in an image needs to be classified.

arxiv-2410-04659.title: ActiView: Evaluating Active Perception Ability for Multimodal Large Language Models
arxiv-2410-04659.creator: Ziyue Wang, Chi Chen, Fuwen Luo, Yurui Dong, Yuanchi Zhang, Yuzhuang Xu, Xiaolong Wang, Peng Li, Yang Liu
arxiv-2410-04659.description: Abstract Active perception, a crucial human capability, involves setting a goal based on the current understanding of the environment and performing actions to achieve that goal. Despite significant efforts in evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), active perception has been largely overlooked. To address this gap, we propose a novel benchmark named ActiView to evaluate active perception in MLLMs.

arxiv-2411-01903.title: Superspace invariants and correlators in 𝟒 ​ d 4d 𝒩 = 𝟏 \mathcal{N}=1 superconformal field theories
arxiv-2411-01903.creator: Aditya Jain and Amin A. Nizami
arxiv-2411-01903.description: Abstract Using polarization spinor methods in conjunction with the superspace formalism, we construct 3-point superconformal invariants that are used to determine the form of 3-point correlators of spinning superfield operators in 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 superconformal field theories (SCFTs) in 4-dimensions.

arxiv-2509-26043.title: Enabling Time-Aware Priority Traffic Management over Distributed FPGA Nodes
arxiv-2509-26043.creator: Alberto Scionti, Paolo Savio, Francesco Lubrano, Federico Stirano, Antonino Nespola, Olivier Terzo, Corrado De Sio, Luca Sterpone
arxiv-2509-26043.description: Abstract Network Interface Cards (NICs) greatly evolved from simple basic devices moving traffic in and out of the network to complex heterogeneous systems offloading host CPUs from performing complex tasks on in-transit packets. These latter comprise different types of devices, ranging from NICs accelerating fixed specific functions (e.g., on-the-fly data compression/decompression, checksum computation, data encryption, etc.

arxiv-2602-09286.title: Human Control Is the Anchor, Not the Answer: Early Divergence of Oversight in Agentic AI Communities
arxiv-2602-09286.creator: Hanjing Shi, Dominic DiFranzo
arxiv-2602-09286.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Hanjing Shi, Dominic DiFranzo. As agentic AI systems move from demonstrations to everyday use, early communities begin negotiating oversight concerns: control, boundaries, and accountability, almost immediately, yet without converging on a shared understanding. We present a comparative analysis of two newly formed Reddit communities associated with distinct agent-native ecosystems: r/openclaw , oriented toward agent deployment and operational use, and r/moltbook , oriented toward agent-centered social interaction.

pmc-11591829.title: Influence of Subjective Postural Vertical with Closed and Open Eyes in Patients with Hemiplegic and Pusher Behavior with Unilateral Spatial Neglect After Stroke: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-11591829.creator: Kota Sawa, Kazu Amimoto, Takuya Miyamoto, Miko Tamura, Guido Gainotti, Lisa Arduino
pmc-11591829.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: When integrating visual and somatosensory processing into the subjective postural vertical using the Romberg test, patients with hemiplegic can be sorted into either post-stroke or pushers with unilateral spatial neglect (USN). This study aimed to clarify the characteristics of the integrated processing of the integrated subjective postural vertical (ISPV) with open or closed eyes in patients with hemiplegic and/or pusher with USN. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 91 patients with hemiplegic and 45 with pusher and USN.

pmc-12973897.title: Anti-CGRP receptor antibodies do not modulate trigeminal pain processing: indication for distinct mechanisms of CGRP pathway blockade
pmc-12973897.creator: Kuan-Po Peng, Hauke Basedau, Karl Messlinger, Arne May
pmc-12973897.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMonoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting calcitonin gene-related peptides (CGRP) are established therapies for migraine. There are currently four CGRP-mAbs available on the market: one targets the CGRP receptor, and the other three target the CGRP ligand. Despite the initial comparability of the two groups regarding efficacy, real-life data demonstrate that up to 30% of non-responders to one class exhibit a positive response to switching classes, indicating different mechanisms. The ligand-mAb, galcanezumab, has previously demonstrated a trigeminal dermatome-specific pain modulatory effect.

pmc-13052010.title: HIF‐1α/Netrin‐4 Axis Mediates RIPC‐Induced Angiogenesis and Neurogenesis After Ischemic Stroke
pmc-13052010.creator: Zhaowei Feng, Zhenqian Liu, Siyu Tang, Meihua Pan, Kaishen Zhu, Yiwei Liu, Chunyu Wang, Ruiqin Yao, Xiue Wei, Haiyan Liu
pmc-13052010.description: Remote ischemic postconditioning (RIPC) confers neuroprotection in ischemic stroke partly via promoting angiogenesis and neurogenesis, but its precise molecular mechanisms remain unclear; here, we investigated the role of the secreted guidance protein Netrin‐4 (NTN4) and its upstream regulator hypoxia‐inducible factor 1α (HIF‐1α) in mediating RIPC's reparative effects, using endothelial‐specific Ntn4 knockout (KO) mice subjected to transient middle cerebral artery occlusion

pmc-13591162.title: Use of Noninvasive Biomarker Tests vs. FibroScan for Predicting Significant Fibrosis in Egyptian Pediatric Cancer Survivors with Chronic Hepatitis C Virus Infection
pmc-13591162.creator: Dalia N Toaima, Fatma A Marzouk, Alaa El-Haddad, Aisha Elsharkawy, Gamal E Esmat, Manal H El-Sayed
pmc-13591162.description: Egyptian children undergoing chemotherapy are at high risk of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection because of immunosuppression and multiple blood transfusions. This study evaluated liver fibrosis by comparing transient elastography with aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and fibrosis index based on four factors (FIB-4) in pediatric cancer survivors with chronic HCV infection.
